observation: The whole set in the opening position, both armies and both trays. Every piece is where the rules put it: eight worlds on white discs at the Sol end and their eight mirrors on black discs at the Anti-Sol end, the twelve cocoa-brown belt tiles filling b4-c6 and e4-f6 across the middle, three corona cells and a den plug at each end, and the two trays lying clear of the board. Nothing floats, nothing intersects anything else, and every tile and plug sits flush in its own pocket -- the top view shows each terrain tile filling its cell with the panel's rib visible all round it. The rank ladder reads at a glance in the front view: Mercury is the smallest ball on the near rank and Jupiter the largest, and the sizes step monotonically between them on identical Ø34.00 discs. Saturn is the only piece whose ring breaks its own silhouette, and it leans the opposite way on the two armies, which is the ownership cue working. Venus, the world this revision corrects, is now a saturated amber ball rather than a pale cream one, and the pale sinuous highland across its middle is legible even at board scale in both the front and the iso view. There is no orange anywhere on it. It is not confusable with Saturn: Saturn's globe is half again as wide, carries four strong brown belts and a ring, and Venus carries neither. The only other sunflower_yellow in the frame is the Sol den plug, which is a flat square plinth with two flames rising off the board edge and shares nothing but its hue with a ball on a disc.
